source.text: וָאֶשָּׂ֥א אֶת־עֵינַ֖י וָאֵ֑רֶא וְהִנֵּ֖ה אַרְבַּ֥ע קְרָנֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And I lifted up my eyes and saw, and look, four horns.

en.L: And I lifted up my eyes and saw, and look, four horns!
en.B: Then I looked up, and I saw four horns.
en.R: Then I looked up and saw four horns.

pt.L: E levantei os meus olhos e vi, e eis que quatro chifres!
pt.B: Então olhei para cima e vi quatro chifres.
pt.R: Então olhei para cima e vi quatro chifres.

decisions.choice: This verse is 2:1 in the Hebrew text, 1:18 in many Bibles
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text begins chapter 2 with the second vision, so that chapter 1 holds only the first. Many Bibles end chapter 1 with this vision, numbering 2:1-4 as 1:18-21, and then begin their chapter 2 with the man with the measuring line (Hebrew 2:5), so their 2:1-13 is 2:5-17 here. Open Word Bible follows the numbering of the Hebrew text it translates, and Zechariah is cited by the Hebrew numbers.

decisions.choice: the second vision: four horns, and four craftsmen who throw them down
decisions.reason: A horn is the strength of an animal, and in the Bible it stands for power, especially the power of kings and nations (Psalm 75:5-6, 11; 1 Kings 22:11; Daniel 8:20-22). The angel explains that the horns are the powers that scattered God's people (verse 2), and the craftsmen are sent to throw them down (verse 4). The angel does not name the nations. Four is the number of the four directions (2:10; 6:5), so the horns may stand for every power, from every side, that had attacked Judah.

decisions.choice: I lifted up my eyes and saw: I looked up and saw something new
decisions.reason: The phrase marks the start of a new scene in a vision (2:5; 5:1; 6:1), as it does in stories (Genesis 18:2; 22:13).

decisions.choice: I looked up (B, R); look (L)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "looked up" for the idiom, and leave out "look", which only points to what was seen. The horns keep their name at every level, as set for Zechariah's visions.

decisions.choice: levantei os meus olhos e vi (L); olhei para cima e vi (B, R); chifres
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew phrase that opens a new scene (m3), and Balanced and Readable say "olhei para cima", as the English does (r-en-1); the same words return in 2:5, 5:1, 5:9 and 6:1. "Chifres" is the plain word for animals' horns, which stand for power (m2); "pontas", the old word, is not understood today.

source.text: וָאֹמַ֗ר אֶל־הַמַּלְאָ֛ךְ הַדֹּבֵ֥ר בִּ֖י מָה־אֵ֑לֶּה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י אֵ֤לֶּה הַקְּרָנוֹת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר זֵר֣וּ אֶת־יְהוּדָ֔ה אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וִירוּשָׁלָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And I said to the angel who talks with me, What [are] these? And he said to me, These [are] the horns which scattered Judah, Israel and Jerusalem.

en.L: And I said to the angel who talked with me, "What [are] these?" And he said to me, "These [are] the horns that scattered Judah, Israel and Jerusalem."
en.B: I asked the angel who talked with me what they were. He answered, "These are the horns that scattered Judah, Israel and Jerusalem."
en.R: I asked the angel who talked with me what they were. He told me, "These are the horns that scattered Judah, Israel and Jerusalem."

pt.L: E eu disse ao anjo que falava comigo: "Que [são] estes?" E ele me disse: "Estes [são] os chifres que dispersaram Judá, Israel e Jerusalém."
pt.B: Perguntei ao anjo que falava comigo o que eram aqueles chifres. Ele respondeu: "Estes são os chifres que dispersaram Judá, Israel e Jerusalém."
pt.R: Perguntei ao anjo que falava comigo o que eles eram. Ele me disse: "Estes são os chifres que espalharam o povo de Judá, de Israel e de Jerusalém."

decisions.choice: scattered: drove the people into exile
decisions.reason: The verb is used for winnowing grain, tossing it so that the wind carries off the chaff (Isaiah 30:24), and for the scattering of the people among the nations (Jeremiah 31:10; Ezekiel 5:10). The horns are the powers that sent God's people into exile.

decisions.choice: Judah, Israel and Jerusalem: the whole people of God
alternatives: Israel as the northern kingdom, scattered by Assyria
decisions.reason: Israel may be the northern kingdom, which Assyria took into exile (2 Kings 17:6), named beside Judah and its capital, which Babylon destroyed. It may also be the name of the whole people. Either way, the three names cover all of God's people who were scattered. Verse 4 names Judah alone.

decisions.choice: These are the horns ... (every level)
decisions.reason: As set for Zechariah's visions, the angel's explanation is translated as he gives it, and no level adds who the horns are.

decisions.choice: espalharam o povo de (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says that it was the people who were scattered (m1), since "espalhar Judá" would picture the land itself spread about; Literal and Balanced keep "dispersaram Judá".

records.literal_gloss: And showed me Yahweh four craftsmen.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} showed me four craftsmen.
en.B: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} showed me four craftsmen.
en.R: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} showed me four skilled workers.

pt.L: E {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} me mostrou quatro artesãos.
pt.B: Então {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} me mostrou quatro artesãos.
pt.R: Então {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} me mostrou quatro trabalhadores habilidosos.

decisions.choice: craftsmen: skilled workers in wood, stone or metal
decisions.reason: The word is used for craftsmen of every kind (Exodus 35:35; Isaiah 44:12-13). Here they are probably workers with tools of iron, smiths who could cut or break off horns, though the text does not say what kind.

decisions.choice: the LORD himself showed me
decisions.reason: In most of the visions Zechariah simply sees, or the angel shows him. Here the LORD is the one who shows him, as he does in 3:1 (and compare Amos 7:1, 4, 7). The vision comes from God, not from Zechariah's own mind.

decisions.choice: skilled workers (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "skilled workers", a common phrase for people who work with their hands at a trade. The image is kept.

decisions.choice: artesãos (L, B); trabalhadores habilidosos (R)
decisions.reason: The word covers workers of every trade (m1), so "artesãos" keeps it open, as the English "craftsmen" does; Readable says "trabalhadores habilidosos", as the English Readable does (r-en-1). "Ferreiros" would decide what the text leaves open.

source.text: וָאֹמַ֕ר מָ֛ה אֵ֥לֶּה בָאִ֖ים לַֽעֲשׂ֑וֹת וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לֵאמֹ֗ר אֵ֣לֶּה הַקְּרָנ֞וֹת אֲשֶׁר־זֵ֣רוּ אֶת־יְהוּדָ֗ה כְּפִי־אִישׁ֙ לֹא־נָשָׂ֣א רֹאשׁ֔וֹ וַיָּבֹ֤אוּ אֵ֨לֶּה֙ לְהַחֲרִ֣יד אֹתָ֔ם לְיַדּ֞וֹת אֶת־קַרְנ֣וֹת הַגּוֹיִ֗ם הַנֹּשְׂאִ֥ים קֶ֛רֶן אֶל־אֶ֥רֶץ יְהוּדָ֖ה לְזָרוֹתָֽהּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And I said, What [are] these coming to do? And he said, saying, These [are] the horns which scattered Judah, according to [the] mouth of [a] man not he lifted his head; and have come these to terrify them, to cast down [the] horns of the nations who lift a horn against [the] land of Judah to scatter it.

en.L: And I said, "What are these coming to do?" And he said, "These [are] the horns that scattered Judah, so that no one lifted up {{gender:their|his}} head; and these have come to terrify them, to throw down the horns of the nations that lifted up a horn against the land of Judah to scatter it."
en.B: I asked, "What are these coming to do?" He said, "Those are the horns that scattered Judah so completely that no one could raise {{gender:their|his}} head. But these craftsmen have come to terrify them, to throw down the horns of the nations that raised their horns against the land of Judah to scatter its people."
en.R: I asked, "What are these workers coming to do?" He said, "Those horns scattered the people of Judah so badly that no one could even lift {{gender:their|his}} head. These workers have come to terrify them and knock down the horns of the nations. Those nations raised their horns against the land of Judah to scatter its people."

pt.L: E eu disse: "O que estes vêm fazer?" E ele disse: "Estes [são] os chifres que dispersaram Judá, de modo que ninguém levantou a cabeça; e estes vieram para aterrorizá-los, para derrubar os chifres das nações que levantaram o chifre contra a terra de Judá para dispersá-la."
pt.B: Perguntei: "O que estes vêm fazer?" Ele disse: "Aqueles são os chifres que dispersaram Judá tão completamente que ninguém podia levantar a cabeça. Mas estes artesãos vieram para aterrorizá-los e derrubar os chifres das nações que levantaram os seus chifres contra a terra de Judá para dispersar o seu povo."
pt.R: Perguntei: "O que esses trabalhadores vêm fazer?" Ele disse: "Aqueles chifres espalharam o povo de Judá de um jeito tão terrível que ninguém conseguia nem levantar a cabeça. Estes trabalhadores vieram para assustar as nações e derrubar os chifres delas. Essas nações levantaram os seus chifres contra a terra de Judá para espalhar o seu povo."

decisions.choice: so that no one lifted up his head: so completely that everyone was crushed and humbled
decisions.reason: "According to the mouth of a man" means "in proportion to", here "to such a degree that". Not lifting the head is a picture of defeat and shame (Judges 8:28; Job 10:15). The scattering left no one able to stand up straight.

decisions.choice: lifted up a horn against: rose up in proud strength against
decisions.reason: To lift up the horn is to act with power, often with arrogance (Psalm 75:5-6). The nations that raised their horns against Judah will have their horns thrown down.

decisions.choice: to throw down: to cast down and destroy the horns
decisions.reason: The verb usually means to throw or cast (Lamentations 3:53, of stones). Here it is used of horns, so it may mean to knock them down or cut them off. Either way the power of the nations is broken.

decisions.choice: to terrify them: the craftsmen frighten the horns, that is, the nations they stand for
decisions.reason: The word "them" has no clear reference in the Hebrew. It most likely points to the horns or the nations behind them. The angel does not say who the craftsmen are; the vision says only that God has agents ready to break every power that harmed his people.

decisions.choice: these craftsmen (B); these workers (R); its people (B, R); the gender setting
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "these", and the reader needs to know that the craftsmen are meant. "Scatter it" means scattering the land's people, as Balanced and Readable say. "No one lifted his head" means men and women alike, so the pronoun takes the gender setting. Readable splits the long explanation into sentences but keeps the horns.

decisions.choice: ninguém levantou a cabeça (no gender span)
decisions.reason: The English puts "their/his head" under the gender setting. Portuguese says "ninguém levantou a cabeça", with no possessive, which is already inclusive (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 7), so there is no span. Readable says "assustar as nações" for "them" (m4), to make the object plain.

source.text: וָאֶשָּׂ֥א עֵינַ֛י וָאֵ֖רֶא וְהִנֵּה־אִ֑ישׁ וּבְיָד֖וֹ חֶ֥בֶל מִדָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And I lifted up my eyes and saw, and look, a man, and in his hand a line of measuring.

en.L: And I lifted up my eyes and saw, and look, a man, and in his hand a measuring line!
en.B: Then I looked up, and there was a man with a measuring line in his hand.
en.R: Then I looked up and saw a man holding a measuring line.

pt.L: E levantei os meus olhos e vi, e eis que um homem, e na sua mão um cordel de medir!
pt.B: Então olhei para cima, e havia um homem com um cordel de medir na mão.
pt.R: Então olhei para cima e vi um homem segurando um cordel de medir.

decisions.choice: This verse is 2:5 in the Hebrew text, 2:1 in many Bibles
decisions.reason: Bibles that number Hebrew 2:1-4 as 1:18-21 begin their chapter 2 here, so Hebrew 2:5-17 is their 2:1-13. See the note at 2:1.

decisions.choice: the third vision: a man with a measuring line, and a city too full for walls
decisions.reason: The man sets out to measure Jerusalem (verse 6), but another angel brings word that the city will spread beyond any wall, because the LORD himself will be its wall and its glory (verses 8-9). The vision takes up the promise of 1:16, that a line will be stretched out over Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: a measuring line: a cord used to measure land and buildings
decisions.reason: The word is a different one from the "line" of 1:16, a length of cord or rope used for measuring (Amos 7:17; Psalm 78:55). Ezekiel also saw a man with a measuring line who measured the temple to come (Ezekiel 40:3).

decisions.choice: there was (B); not shown (R)
decisions.reason: As in 2:1, Balanced and Readable leave out "look" and say what Zechariah saw.

decisions.choice: um cordel de medir (every level)
decisions.reason: A different Hebrew word from the "line" of 1:16 (m3), but the same thing, so Portuguese keeps "cordel de medir", the words Jeremiah 31:39 uses, at every level.

source.text: וָאֹמַ֕ר אָ֖נָה אַתָּ֣ה הֹלֵ֑ךְ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י לָמֹד֙ אֶת־יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם לִרְא֥וֹת כַּמָּֽה־רָחְבָּ֖הּ וְכַמָּ֥ה אָרְכָּֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And I said, Where [are] you going? And he said to me, To measure Jerusalem, to see how much [is] its breadth and how much its length.

en.L: And I said, "Where are you going?" And he said to me, "To measure Jerusalem, to see what its width [is] and what its length [is]."
en.B: I asked, "Where are you going?" He answered, "To measure Jerusalem, to find out how wide and how long it is."
en.R: I asked him, "Where are you going?" He answered, "I am going to measure Jerusalem. I want to see how wide and how long it is."

pt.L: E eu disse: "Aonde você vai?" E ele me disse: "Medir Jerusalém, para ver qual [é] a sua largura e qual [é] o seu comprimento."
pt.B: Perguntei: "Aonde você vai?" Ele respondeu: "Vou medir Jerusalém, para saber qual é a sua largura e qual é o seu comprimento."
pt.R: Perguntei a ele: "Aonde você está indo?" Ele respondeu: "Vou medir Jerusalém. Quero ver qual é a largura e o comprimento da cidade."

decisions.choice: to measure Jerusalem: to mark out the size of the city
decisions.reason: The man does not say why he measures. Measuring was the first step in laying out walls and buildings. The next verses show that the city to come cannot be held within any measured walls.

decisions.choice: I am going to ... I want to see (R)
decisions.reason: Readable turns the short answer into two full sentences.

decisions.choice: você (Zechariah to the man)
decisions.reason: Zechariah speaks to the man with the measuring line as one person to another, with "você"; he keeps "meu senhor" and "o senhor" for the angel who explains the visions, whom he addresses as a superior (1:9).

source.text: וְהִנֵּ֗ה הַמַּלְאָ֛ךְ הַדֹּבֵ֥ר בִּ֖י יֹצֵ֑א וּמַלְאָ֣ךְ אַחֵ֔ר יֹצֵ֖א לִקְרָאתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And look, the angel who talks with me [was] going out, and another angel [was] going out to meet him.

en.L: And look, the angel who talked with me was going out, and another angel was coming out to meet him.
en.B: Then the angel who talked with me stepped forward, and another angel came out to meet him.
en.R: Then the angel who talked with me left, and another angel came to meet him.

pt.L: E eis que o anjo que falava comigo estava saindo, e outro anjo saía ao encontro dele.
pt.B: Então o anjo que falava comigo se adiantou, e outro anjo saiu ao encontro dele.
pt.R: Então o anjo que falava comigo saiu, e outro anjo veio se encontrar com ele.

decisions.choice: going out: coming forward in the vision
decisions.reason: The verse does not say where the angels came from or went. One angel steps forward, and a second comes out to meet him with a message. The verb is the same for both.

decisions.choice: Then (B, R) for "and look"
decisions.reason: "Look" marks something new in the vision; Balanced and Readable show it with "then". The verb for both angels is the same; Literal says "coming out" for the second only because he comes toward the first.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔ורֻ֗ץ דַּבֵּ֛ר אֶל־הַנַּ֥עַר הַלָּ֖ז לֵאמֹ֑ר פְּרָזוֹת֙ תֵּשֵׁ֣ב יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם מֵרֹ֥ב אָדָ֛ם וּבְהֵמָ֖ה בְּתוֹכָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to him, Run, speak to this young man, saying, Unwalled villages Jerusalem will be inhabited, from [the] multitude of people and livestock in its midst.

en.L: And he said to him, "Run, speak to this young man, saying, '[As] open villages Jerusalem will be inhabited, because of the multitude of people and livestock in it.
en.B: He said to him, "Run, tell that young man: 'Jerusalem will be inhabited like villages without walls, because of the great number of people and animals in it.
en.R: He told him, "Run to that young man and tell him, 'Jerusalem will be like a village with no walls around it, because so many people and animals will live there.

pt.L: E ele lhe disse: "Corra, fale a este jovem, dizendo: '[Como] aldeias abertas Jerusalém será habitada, por causa da multidão de pessoas e de animais no meio dela.
pt.B: Ele lhe disse: "Corra e diga àquele jovem: 'Jerusalém será habitada como as aldeias sem muralhas, por causa do grande número de pessoas e de animais que haverá nela.
pt.R: Ele disse ao outro anjo: "Corra até aquele jovem e diga a ele: 'Jerusalém vai ser como uma aldeia sem muralhas em volta, porque muitas pessoas e muitos animais vão morar ali.

decisions.choice: one angel tells the other to run to Zechariah, the young man
alternatives: the young man is the man with the measuring line
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "he said to him". Most likely the second angel sends the angel who talked with Zechariah back to him with the message. "This young man" is most likely Zechariah himself, who must pass the word on; some take him to be the man with the measuring line, who needs to know that Jerusalem cannot be measured. The message is the same either way.

decisions.choice: open villages: settlements without walls
decisions.reason: The word means open country towns with no walls (Ezekiel 38:11; Esther 9:19). Jerusalem will be like them, not because it is weak but because it will be too full of people and flocks for any wall to hold.

decisions.choice: people and livestock: a city full of life and wealth
decisions.reason: Flocks and herds were a family's wealth. A city with many people and animals is a prosperous one. In Zechariah's day, Jerusalem had few people and its walls were in ruins (compare Nehemiah 1:3; 7:4).

decisions.choice: that young man (B, R); like villages without walls (B); like a village with no walls around it (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "that young man", since the speaker is pointing to someone else. They add "like", to make plain that Jerusalem will be like open villages, not turned into them. The message to be passed on is in single quotation marks and closes at the end of verse 9.

decisions.choice: este jovem (L), aquele jovem (B, R); aldeias abertas (L), aldeias sem muralhas (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Jovem" for the young man (m1), the neutral word; "rapaz" is everyday speech. The open villages (m2) are "aldeias abertas" at Literal and "sem muralhas" at Balanced and Readable, the word for a city's walls; one angel speaks to another with "você" ("Corra").

source.text: וַאֲנִ֤י אֶֽהְיֶה־לָּהּ֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה ח֥וֹמַת אֵ֖שׁ סָבִ֑יב וּלְכָב֖וֹד אֶֽהְיֶ֥ה בְתוֹכָֽהּ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And I will be to her, declaration of Yahweh, a wall of fire around, and for glory I will be in her midst.

en.L: And I myself will be for her, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, a wall of fire all around, and I will be the glory in her midst.'"
en.B: And I myself will be a wall of fire around her, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and I will be the glory within her.'"
en.R: I myself will be a wall of fire all around the city, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and I will be its glory there inside it.'"

pt.L: E eu mesmo serei para ela, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, um muro de fogo ao redor, e serei a glória no meio dela.'"
pt.B: E eu mesmo serei um muro de fogo ao redor dela, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, e serei a glória dentro dela.'"
pt.R: Eu mesmo vou ser um muro de fogo em volta da cidade, diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, e vou ser a glória dela, ali dentro.'"

decisions.choice: a wall of fire all around: the LORD himself will protect the city
decisions.reason: The city does not need walls of stone, for the LORD will surround it. The fire recalls the pillar of fire that guarded Israel in the wilderness (Exodus 13:21-22; 14:24) and Isaiah's promise of a glow of fire over Zion (Isaiah 4:5).

decisions.choice: I will be the glory in her midst: the LORD's own presence will return to the city
decisions.reason: Ezekiel saw the glory of the LORD leave the temple and the city before the fall of Jerusalem (Ezekiel 10:18-19; 11:23), and later saw it come back (Ezekiel 43:2-5). Haggai promised that the LORD would fill the new temple with glory (Haggai 2:7, 9). The LORD will not only guard the city from outside; he will live in it.

decisions.choice: I myself: the LORD stresses that he will do it
decisions.reason: The Hebrew begins with the pronoun "I", which it does not need, to stress who will be the city's wall.

decisions.choice: around the city (R); its glory there inside it (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names the city for "her", and makes "for glory" plain as "its glory". The closing marks end the message and the angel's words.

decisions.choice: um muro de fogo; eu mesmo
decisions.reason: "Muro de fogo" at every level, the plain picture (m1); "eu mesmo" gives the stress of the Hebrew pronoun (m3).

source.text: ה֣וֹי ה֗וֹי וְנֻ֛סוּ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ צָפ֖וֹן נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה כִּ֠י כְּאַרְבַּ֞ע רוּח֧וֹת הַשָּׁמַ֛יִם פֵּרַ֥שְׂתִּי אֶתְכֶ֖ם נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Ho, ho, and flee from [the] land of [the] north, declaration of Yahweh, for like [the] four winds of the heavens I have spread you, declaration of Yahweh.

en.L: Ho! Ho! Flee from the land of the north, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q for like the four winds of the heavens I have spread you abroad, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Come! Come! Flee from the land in the north, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q for like the four winds of heaven I have scattered you, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Hurry! Hurry! Run away from the land in the north, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q I scattered you in every direction, like the four winds that blow, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

pt.L: Ei! Ei! Fujam da terra do norte, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, \q porque como os quatro ventos dos céus eu os espalhei, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.
pt.B: Venham! Venham! Fujam da terra do norte, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, \q porque eu os dispersei como os quatro ventos do céu, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.
pt.R: Depressa! Depressa! Fujam da terra do norte, diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}. \q Eu espalhei vocês para todos os lados, como os quatro ventos que sopram, diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.

decisions.choice: 2:10-17: a poem that calls the exiles home and promises the LORD's coming
decisions.reason: After the vision, the prophet speaks in verse: a call to the exiles still in Babylon to flee (verses 10-11), a word against the nations (verses 12-13) and a call to Zion to rejoice because the LORD is coming to live among his people (verses 14-17). The prophet speaks the LORD's words and, in verses 12-15, also of his own sending. As in the other prophets, the poem takes no quotation marks. It is set in lines.

decisions.choice: Ho! Ho!: an urgent call to listen and act
decisions.reason: The word is most often a cry of woe over those facing judgment (Isaiah 5:8), but it is also used to call out to people, as in Isaiah 55:1 ("Ho, everyone who thirsts"). Here it is doubled and followed by "flee", so it is a summons to hurry, not a threat.

decisions.choice: the land of the north: Babylon
decisions.reason: Verse 11 names Babylon. It lay to the east, but armies and travelers from there came into Judah from the north, so the prophets speak of the enemy as coming from the north (Jeremiah 1:14; 6:22). After Cyrus allowed the Jews to return in 538 BC, many stayed in Babylon; the poem calls them to come home.

decisions.choice: like the four winds I have spread you: I scattered you in every direction
alternatives: I will spread you out as widely as the four winds
I will gather you from the four winds
decisions.reason: The verb is in the form for a completed act and usually means to spread out. Read with "flee", it looks back on the exile, when the LORD scattered his people to every quarter, as the wind blows in all directions (Ezekiel 17:21). Some read it as a promise that the LORD will make his people spread out widely in the future. The Greek translation reads "I will gather you from the four winds of heaven", which is a different sense and probably a smoothing of the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: Ho! Ho! (L); Come! Come! (B); Hurry! Hurry! (R); no quotation marks; set in lines
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "Ho", as Isaiah 55:1 does for the same call. Balanced and Readable use a word that a reader hears as a summons, since this is not a cry of woe (m2). The lines follow the main division of the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: Ei! Ei! (L); Venham! Venham! (B); Depressa! Depressa! (R)
decisions.reason: The cry is a summons, not woe (m2), so it is not "Ai". Literal says "Ei", as Isaiah 55:1 has the same call in Portuguese; Balanced and Readable use words a reader hears as a call to come and hurry, as the English does (r-en-1). The exiles are addressed in the plural, "vocês".

records.literal_gloss: Ho, Zion! Escape, inhabitant of daughter Babylon.

en.L: Ho, Zion! \q Escape, you who dwell with the daughter of Babylon!
en.B: Come, Zion! \q Escape, you who live in Daughter Babylon!
en.R: Come, people of Zion! \q Escape, you who live in Babylon!

pt.L: Ei, Sião! \q Escapa, tu que habitas com a filha da Babilônia!
pt.B: Vem, Sião! \q Escapa, tu que moras na filha da Babilônia!
pt.R: Venham, povo de Sião! \q Escapem, vocês que moram na Babilônia!

decisions.choice: Zion: the exiles of Jerusalem still living in Babylon
decisions.reason: Zion is the hill of Jerusalem and so the city and its people. Here it is the part of the people still in exile, called to escape as Isaiah and Jeremiah had called them (Isaiah 48:20; Jeremiah 51:6, 45).

decisions.choice: daughter of Babylon: Babylon pictured as a woman
decisions.reason: Cities are often pictured as women (Isaiah 47:1; Psalm 137:8). "Daughter of Babylon" means Babylon itself, not a daughter of it.

decisions.choice: the daughter of Babylon (L); Daughter Babylon (B); Babylon (R); people of Zion (R)
decisions.reason: The wording follows the table set in Isaiah for such names: "the daughter of Babylon" at Literal, "Daughter Babylon" at Balanced, and the plain name at Readable, which also says "people of Zion". "Ho" is the call of verse 10.

decisions.choice: Sião ... tu (L, B); povo de Sião ... vocês (R); a filha da Babilônia (L, B), a Babilônia (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is feminine singular: Zion is spoken to as one woman, so Literal and Balanced say "tu". Readable says "povo de Sião", as the English Readable does, and so "vocês". "A filha da Babilônia" (m2) at Literal and Balanced is the wording Isaiah 47:1 has in Portuguese; Portuguese does not set "Filha" before a name as a title.

source.text: כִּ֣י כֹ֣ה אָמַר֮ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָאוֹת֒ אַחַ֣ר כָּב֔וֹד שְׁלָחַ֕נִי אֶל־הַגּוֹיִ֖ם הַשֹּׁלְלִ֣ים אֶתְכֶ֑ם כִּ֚י הַנֹּגֵ֣עַ בָּכֶ֔ם נֹגֵ֖עַ בְּבָבַ֥ת עֵינֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: For thus says Yahweh of hosts, after glory he has sent me to the nations who plunder you: for the one touching you touches the pupil of his eye.

en.L: For thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, after glory {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sent me to the nations that plundered you: \q for whoever touches you touches the pupil of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} eye.
en.B: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says this, for the sake of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has sent me against the nations that plundered you: \q whoever touches you touches the pupil of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} eye.
en.R: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says. For the sake of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has sent me against the nations that robbed you. \q Anyone who touches you touches the pupil of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} eye.

pt.L: Porque assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos, depois da glória {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} me enviou às nações que saquearam vocês: \q porque quem toca em vocês toca na pupila do {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} olho.
pt.B: Pois assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos, que, para a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} glória, me enviou contra as nações que saquearam vocês: \q quem toca em vocês toca na menina dos {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} olhos.
pt.R: É isto que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos diz. Para mostrar a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} glória, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} me enviou contra as nações que roubaram vocês. \q Quem toca em vocês toca na menina dos olhos {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}.

decisions.choice: after glory: for the sake of the LORD's glory
alternatives: after the glory appeared, he sent me
decisions.reason: These two words are among the hardest in the book. "After" can mean "behind" or "for the sake of", and "glory" can mean God's glory or honor in general. Read one way, the LORD sent the speaker to the nations for his glory: to win honor for the LORD by bringing judgment. Read another way, the speaker was sent after the glory had been revealed, perhaps the glory promised in verse 9. The translation takes the first; the sense of the verse, that the LORD will act against the nations, is the same.

decisions.choice: sent me: the prophet, sent with this message
alternatives: a figure sent by the LORD
decisions.reason: The speaker says that the LORD of hosts has sent him, and three times adds that when the promise comes true, "you will know that the LORD of hosts has sent me" (verses 13, 15; 4:9; 6:15). This is the test of a true prophet (Deuteronomy 18:21-22), so the speaker is most likely Zechariah. Some read him as the angel, or as a messenger of the LORD whom later readers saw as the Messiah.

decisions.choice: the pupil of his eye: what is most precious and most easily hurt
decisions.reason: The eye is guarded by instinct against the smallest touch. To touch God's people is to strike at what God holds most dear and guards most closely (Deuteronomy 32:10; Psalm 17:8).

decisions.choice: his eye: the LORD's eye
decisions.reason: The word for pupil is found only here. Jewish scribal tradition lists this verse among a few places where the scribes changed "my" to "his" out of reverence, so that the text would not speak of touching God's own eye; the original then said "my eye". The Hebrew as it stands can also be read of the attacker's own eye: whoever harms Israel harms himself. The translation reads it of the LORD, as Deuteronomy 32:10 does. This description of the scribal tradition is written from general knowledge.

decisions.choice: the pupil of his eye (all levels); after glory (L); for the sake of his glory (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Pupil of his eye" is the wording of Deuteronomy 32:10 at each level. "Apple of the eye", an old English idiom, now means a favorite, which is weaker than the picture. Literal keeps "after glory" and leaves its sense open; Balanced and Readable give the sense chosen in m1. "Plundered" (L, B) becomes "robbed" at Readable.

decisions.choice: a pupila do seu olho (L); a menina dos seus olhos (B, R); depois da glória (L); para a sua glória (B, R)
decisions.reason: The picture (m3) keeps the Portuguese of Deuteronomy 32:10 at each level: "a pupila do seu olho" at Literal, "a menina dos seus olhos" at Balanced, the Portuguese name for the pupil, which still carries the picture of what is most precious. Literal keeps the obscure "depois da glória" (m1), as the English does. "Vocês": the people are addressed in the plural here.

source.text: כִּ֠י הִנְנִ֨י מֵנִ֤יף אֶת־יָדִי֙ עֲלֵיהֶ֔םוְהָי֥וּ שָׁלָ֖ל לְעַבְדֵיהֶ֑ם וִֽידַעְתֶּ֕ם כִּֽי־יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁלָחָֽנִי׃ס

records.literal_gloss: For look, I [am] about to wave my hand over them, and they will be plunder for their slaves; and you will know that Yahweh of hosts has sent me.

en.L: For look, I am about to wave {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand over them, and they will be plunder for their own slaves; \q and you shall know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts has sent me.
en.B: I am about to raise {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand against them, and they will be plundered by their own slaves. \q Then you will know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies has sent me.
en.R: I am going to raise {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand to strike them, and they will be robbed by the people they made their slaves. \q Then you will know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies has sent me.

pt.L: Porque eis que estou para agitar a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} mão sobre elas, e elas serão despojo para os seus próprios escravos; \q e vocês saberão que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos me enviou.
pt.B: Vou levantar a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} mão contra elas, e elas serão saqueadas pelos seus próprios escravos. \q Então vocês saberão que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos me enviou.
pt.R: Vou levantar a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} mão para castigar essas nações, e elas vão ser roubadas pelas pessoas que elas fizeram de escravas. \q Então vocês vão saber que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos me enviou.

decisions.choice: wave my hand over them: raise the hand to strike
decisions.reason: To wave or shake the hand over someone is a threatening gesture before a blow (Isaiah 11:15; 19:16). Here the LORD is the one who raises his hand against the nations.

decisions.choice: my hand ... sent me: the LORD speaks, and then his messenger
decisions.reason: "My hand" is the LORD's, but "the LORD of hosts has sent me" is said by the messenger. The prophet passes from speaking the LORD's words to speaking about his own task without a break, as prophets often do.

decisions.choice: plunder for their own slaves: the nations' power will be turned upside down
decisions.reason: The nations that plundered God's people (verse 12) will be plundered by those they had made their slaves. The reversal is like Isaiah 14:2.

decisions.choice: slaves, at every level
decisions.reason: The style guide keeps "slave" at every level where slavery itself is the point. Here the masters are plundered by the people they had enslaved, and "servants" would hide the reversal.

decisions.choice: escravos (every level)
decisions.reason: As the English (r-en-1) and the Old Testament terms: "escravo" at every level where slavery itself is the point, here the masters plundered by those they had enslaved (m3).

source.text: רָנִּ֥י וְשִׂמְחִ֖י בַּת־צִיּ֑וֹן כִּ֧י הִנְנִי־בָ֛א וְשָׁכַנְתִּ֥י בְתוֹכֵ֖ךְ נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Shout for joy and rejoice, daughter of Zion, for look, I [am] coming and I will dwell in your midst, declaration of Yahweh.

en.L: Shout for joy and rejoice, daughter of Zion, \q for look, I am coming, and I will dwell in your midst, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Sing and rejoice, Daughter Zion, \q for I am coming to live among you, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: People of Zion, sing and be glad! \q I am coming, and I will live among you, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

pt.L: Grita de alegria e alegra-te, filha de Sião, \q porque eis que eu venho e habitarei no meio de ti, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.
pt.B: Canta e alegra-te, filha de Sião, \q porque eu venho morar no meio de ti, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.
pt.R: Povo de Sião, cantem e fiquem alegres! \q Eu estou vindo e vou morar no meio de vocês, diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.

decisions.choice: I am coming and I will dwell in your midst: the LORD's own presence among his people
decisions.reason: The verb "dwell" is the one used for the LORD's living among Israel in the tabernacle (Exodus 25:8; 29:45-46). Ezekiel had promised that he would live among his people forever (Ezekiel 43:7, 9). The promise returns in 8:3.

decisions.choice: shout for joy and rejoice, daughter of Zion
decisions.reason: Zephaniah 3:14-15 calls Zion to sing and rejoice because the LORD is in her midst, and Zechariah 9:9 repeats the call when Zion's king comes. On "daughter of Zion", see the note at Isaiah 1:8.

decisions.choice: daughter of Zion (L); Daughter Zion (B); people of Zion (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording from Isaiah. Balanced and Readable leave out "look", and Readable says "live among you" for "dwell in your midst".

decisions.choice: filha de Sião ... tu (L, B); povo de Sião ... vocês (R)
decisions.reason: The wording Isaiah 1:8 sets in Portuguese: "a filha de Sião" at Literal and Balanced, spoken to with "tu" as one woman; Readable says "povo de Sião", as the English Readable does, and so "vocês" (also verse 15). Zephaniah 3:14 and Zechariah 9:9 make the same call.

source.text: וְנִלְווּ֩ גוֹיִ֨ם רַבִּ֤ים אֶל־יְהוָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא וְהָ֥יוּ לִ֖י לְעָ֑ם וְשָׁכַנְתִּ֣י בְתוֹכֵ֔ךְ וְיָדַ֕עַתְּ כִּי־יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁלָחַ֥נִי אֵלָֽיִךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And will join themselves many nations to Yahweh in that day, and they will become for me a people; and I will dwell in your midst, and you will know that Yahweh of hosts has sent me to you.

en.L: And many nations will join themselves to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in that day, and they will be a people for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; \q and I will dwell in your midst, and you shall know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts has sent me to you.
en.B: Many nations will join themselves to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on that day and will become {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people. \q I will live among you, and you will know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies has sent me to you.
en.R: At that time many nations will join themselves to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and become {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people. \q I will live among you. Then you will know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies has sent me to you.

pt.L: E muitas nações se unirão {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}} naquele dia, e serão para {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} um povo; \q e habitarei no meio de ti, e saberás que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos me enviou a ti.
pt.B: Naquele dia, muitas nações se unirão {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}} e se tornarão o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo. \q Morarei no meio de ti, e saberás que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos me enviou a ti.
pt.R: Naquele dia, muitas nações vão se unir {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}} e vão se tornar o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo. \q Vou morar no meio de vocês. Então vocês vão saber que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos me enviou a vocês.

decisions.choice: many nations will join themselves to the LORD and become his people
decisions.reason: The same verb is used of foreigners who "join themselves to the LORD" in Isaiah 56:3, 6. The words "they will be my people" are the words of God's covenant with Israel (Jeremiah 31:33; Zechariah 8:8); here they include the nations. The same hope closes the book's first half (8:20-23).

decisions.choice: for me ... has sent me: the LORD speaks, then the messenger
decisions.reason: As in verse 13, "me" first refers to the LORD and then to the one he has sent. "You" is feminine singular: Zion is addressed.

decisions.choice: in that day (L); on that day (B); at that time (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this phrase in the prophets.

decisions.choice: naquele dia (every level)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the phrase is "naquele dia" at every level, the wording Isaiah 2:11 sets in Portuguese, where the English Readable says "at that time" (r-en-1).

source.text: וְנָחַ֨ל יְהוָ֤ה אֶת־יְהוּדָה֙ חֶלְק֔וֹ עַ֖ל אַדְמַ֣ת הַקֹּ֑דֶשׁ וּבָחַ֥ר ע֖וֹד בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And will inherit Yahweh Judah [as] his portion on the land the holy, and he will choose again Jerusalem.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will inherit Judah [as] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} portion upon the holy land, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will again choose Jerusalem.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will possess Judah as {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} share in the holy land, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will once again choose Jerusalem.
en.R: Judah will belong to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own share in the holy land. \q He will choose Jerusalem again.

pt.L: E {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} herdará Judá [como] a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} porção sobre a terra santa, \q e ainda escolherá Jerusalém.
pt.B: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} tomará posse de Judá como a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} parte na terra santa \q e de novo escolherá Jerusalém.
pt.R: Judá vai pertencer {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}} como a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} parte na terra santa. \q Ele vai escolher Jerusalém de novo.

decisions.choice: inherit Judah as his portion: claim Judah as his own share
decisions.reason: The verb means to receive or hold as one's inheritance. Deuteronomy 32:9 says, "The LORD's portion is his people". Here the LORD claims Judah again as his own.

decisions.choice: the holy land: the land made holy by the LORD's presence
decisions.reason: This is the only place in the Bible where the land is called "the holy land". It is holy because the LORD will live there (verses 14-15).

decisions.choice: he will again choose Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The promise of 1:17 repeated; see the note there.

decisions.choice: Judah will belong to the LORD (R)
decisions.reason: Readable makes Judah the subject, which says the same thing in plainer words.

source.text: הַ֥ס כָּל־בָּשָׂ֖ר מִפְּנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כִּ֥י נֵע֖וֹר מִמְּע֥וֹן קָדְשֽׁוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Hush, all flesh, before Yahweh, for he has roused himself from [the] dwelling of his holiness.

en.L: Hush, all flesh, before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has roused {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy dwelling.
en.B: Be silent before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, all people, \q for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has risen up from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy dwelling.
en.R: Everyone, be silent before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! \q He has gotten up and come out from the holy place where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} lives.

pt.L: Silêncio, toda carne, diante {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, \q porque {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} se levantou da {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} santa morada.
pt.B: Fiquem em silêncio diante {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, toda a humanidade, \q porque {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} se levantou da {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} santa morada.
pt.R: Todos, fiquem quietos diante {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}! \q Ele se levantou e saiu do lugar santo onde {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} mora.

decisions.choice: be silent before the LORD: hushed awe before God who is about to act
decisions.reason: The same call is found in Habakkuk 2:20 and Zephaniah 1:7. Silence is the response of creatures when God comes to act.

decisions.choice: all flesh: all humankind
decisions.reason: "Flesh" stands for human beings in their weakness and mortality, as in Joel 3:1. Every person, in every nation, is to be still.

decisions.choice: he has roused himself from his holy dwelling: the LORD has risen to act
decisions.reason: The verb is used of waking up or stirring oneself to action (Psalm 44:24; Isaiah 51:9). The LORD's holy dwelling is heaven (Deuteronomy 26:15; Jeremiah 25:30). He is coming out to do what he has promised.

decisions.choice: all flesh (L); all people (B); everyone (R)
decisions.reason: As set for Joel 3:1, Literal keeps "all flesh", and the other levels say what it means. Readable says "gotten up and come out" for "roused himself", to make the picture plain.

decisions.choice: Silêncio (L), Fiquem em silêncio (B), Fiquem quietos (R); toda carne (L), toda a humanidade (B), Todos (R)
decisions.reason: The call (m1) keeps the words Zephaniah 1:7 has in Portuguese at each level, and "all flesh" (m2) the words of Joel 3:1: "toda carne" at Literal, "toda a humanidade" at Balanced.
